title: How Long, O Lord, His Brother's Blood
description: How Long, O Lord, His Brother's Blood in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: William Gaskell wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 185, “Peace”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How long, O Lord, his broth-er's blood Shall man in bat-tle spill? How long that man-date be with-stood, Which cries, "Thou shalt not kill?"

lines: How long, O Lord, his brother's blood
How long that mandate be withstood,
How long shall glory still be found
Where misery walks, a giant crowned,
O, hush, great God! the sounds of war,
That he, with Thee, is noblest far,
Who would his foes as brethren own,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: William Gaskell died in 1884.
credits: Words by William Gaskell (1805–1884), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
